pr_title: Bluetooth: host: rework multiple GATT notifications
pr_body:
Fixes #40664.

See individual commit messages for a description of the changes.
pr_comments:
@alwa-nordic fixed my blunders, no more busfaults now :)

Tested with the shell:
- notification batching
- flushing of the current queue when calling the multi api (using a the highest possible flush timeout)
- cb being called num_attr times
- disabling of the batching by setting `CONFIG_BT_GATT_NOTIFY_MULTIPLE_FLUSH_MS=0`
@alwa-nordic can you take a final look ?

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: GATT: EATT:  Multiple notify feature not utilize new PDU fully
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem?**
Bluetooth 5.2 introduced Multiple Handle Value Notification (HVN) sub-feature as part of Enhanced ATT feature.
Zephyr host currently supports multi HVN but it does not utilize new ATT PDU of `ATT_MULTIPLE_HANDLE_VALUE_NTF=0x23`  fully. It is sending only one HVN per PDU, and it is no different then existing regular single HVN with `ATT_HANDLE_VALUE_NTF=0x1B`.

Core Spec 5 .3 | Vol 3, Part F, 3.4.7.4 section describes as this new PDU allows to the GATT server to send the values of two or more attributes in a single PDU in the list of tuples of `(handle, len, value)`. So this new sub-feature should be supporting multiple HVN in one PDU.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Currently, Multiple HVN is sent with `bt_gatt_notify_multiple()` API that takes list of HVN info. But it is sending them in separate PDU iterating through them. Instead, it should be sent in single PDU as much as they fits.

review_comments: Please add a NULL-check for `default_conn` for this command as well, since we are now expecting it to be non-NULL
In case we fail the `if (!(chrc->properties & BT_GATT_CHRC_NOTIFY))` check later, do we need to clean anything up here?

I think so, good catch.
edit: now, I'm not so sure, I haven't seen weird behaviors when spamming notifications when testing and the alloc & free functions are private to att.c. Could you comment @hermabe ?

I think we should just inline the code in this function. It leads to some not-beautiful code; like `num_params-1`. Casting user data is a somewhat unsafe operation, that can benefit from visibility. It can be expressed as a simple one-liner `bt_att_tx_meta_data(buf)->attr_count +=`. And the reasoning employed to justify the lack of overflow protection implies that this function shall only be used for notify multi, so it is of limited use.
As discussed with @jori-nordic, this function is needed to avoid exposing `struct bt_att_tx_meta` outside `att.c`.
What if `CONFIG_BT_GATT_NOTIFY_MULTIPLE=n`?

API is not compiled in. What should I do in this case, should the function still be defined and return an error code, or should I let the user have a linker error ? I've seen the latter a lot in zephyr, hence the question.
Oh, right, no this is as it should be :) Better to get compile error than runtime error :D
So `bt_gatt_notify_multiple` will only use a single `ATT_MULTIPLE_HANDLE_VALUE_NTF`, and won't attempt to split it into multiple `ATT_MULTIPLE_HANDLE_VALUE_NTF`?
yes. If the user wants that, it can make use of the normal gatt APIs, which will do the splitting if it runs out of space.
Glad you added this - Although it does kind of warrant the question whether this API is any good :D

Yeah, @alwa-nordic and I hoped we could phase out the automatic uuid lookup in the gatt APIs in general, maybe restricting it even more, e.g. by only accepting the attr value handle. We think would simplify the code, and make what's really happening in the functions more transparent to the user.
What's your take on that ? also tagging @jhedberg for his opinion.

I do not have a good overview of how many use cases we have for using the UUID, but at least `bt_gatt_notify_uuid` is used a lot in LE Audio, but I guess that is also more explicit in terms of using UUID. 

I don't have any strong opinions.
Minor: This function is rather long now (around 140 lines). Consider moving all the parameter validation to a separate function.

agreed, but I'm having trouble seeing the limit between parameter and data validation. like does [the feature support](https://github.com/jori-nordic/zephyr/blob/e1c0e2665228d7142d0cc61f9db762847e49a199/subsys/bluetooth/host/gatt.c#L2646) count as a parameter or does [the total PDU length](https://github.com/jori-nordic/zephyr/blob/e1c0e2665228d7142d0cc61f9db762847e49a199/subsys/bluetooth/host/gatt.c#L2682) also count ?
I would also think that the [callback functions](https://github.com/jori-nordic/zephyr/blob/e1c0e2665228d7142d0cc61f9db762847e49a199/subsys/bluetooth/host/gatt.c#L2665) are considered as function parameters.

If I had to decide somewhere to split, it would be right before allocating the netbuf. What do you think about that ?
Yeah I did this, but kept the PDU building in the main function, as two different error codes could be returned. I think it's clearer now.

Can we end up here while the `nfy_mult_work` has already been scheduled? 

If so, should we reschedule it, or keep the original schedule?

yes, this can happen (and does if using a long flush timeout). I think it's good to reschedule it for power-saving, but maybe it's not clear enough to the user. @alwa-nordic wanted to write some more documentation for the gatt notify APIs, he can mention this behavior.

I guess it'll end up being a power vs time optimization. If we reschedule with e.g. 1ms delay each time, sending e.g. 5 notifications may be delayed up to 5ms (but I guess that's still low compared to typical connection interval).
yeah that's what I was thinking as well. we can always change this later to be a real timeout that's not rescheduled.

We should not reschedule, I think. The API I have in mind says "A notification posted with `bt_gatt_notify_by` will be delayed at most `config_max_delay`".

I believe it is preferable to an API that flushes after a period without activity. Consider: If an applications trickles notifications, those should be delivered in a timely fashion, and not be batched.

You can say that trickling at a rate of once per ms will fill up a PDU quickly, but since the timeout is configurable, the situation can get worse.
Agreed; let's not reschedule (may add a comment in the code as to why we do `k_work_schedule` instead of `k_work_reschedule`)

```suggestion
	/* `k_work_schedule` will not reschedule. This is good because we want the oldest
	 * notification in the batch to determine the timeout, so that there is an upper bound
	 * on the delay of each notification.
	 */
	k_work_schedule(&nfy_mult_work,
			K_MSEC(CONFIG_BT_GATT_NOTIFY_MULTIPLE_FLUSH_MS));
```
Do we need to worry about overflow here?

I don't think we should, because the `ATT_MULTIPLE_HANDLE_VALUE_NTF` PDU is limited to 16-bit total length. So even with 1-byte attr values, we shouldn't exceed 16bits here. That's my reasoning, at least.
Otherwise it's a simple matter of using `u16_add_overflow` with an ASSERT or something if we want to
